methods.label: Classify dice by their exposed faces
methods.explanation:
A die's contribution depends on how many of its faces are exposed, so separate the dice by their positions.

There are \(8\) corner dice, each exposing three faces. Three distinct face numbers sum to at least \(1+2+3=6\).

Each of the \(12\) large edges has one die between its corners. These \(12\) dice each expose two faces, whose numbers sum to at least \(1+2=3\).

There is one face-center die on each of the \(6\) large faces. Each exposes one face, contributing at least \(1\). The remaining die is completely inside and contributes \(0\). These groups account for all \(8+12+6+1=27\) dice without overlap.

We must also check that these smallest contributions are possible. The opposite pairs on a standard die are \((1,6)\), \((2,5)\), and \((3,4)\). Thus faces \(1,2,3\) meet at a vertex, and faces \(1,2\) share an edge. We can orient every corner die to expose \(1,2,3\), every edge-middle die to expose \(1,2\), and every face-center die to expose \(1\). Each die can be oriented independently before gluing.

Therefore the smallest possible sum is
\[
8(6)+12(3)+6(1)=48+36+6=90,
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
